# Load packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("amt", "lubridate", 
              "SDLfilter", "sf",
              "terra", "suncalc",
              "beepr", "tictoc")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

```

# Import GPS tracking data

```{r}
#| label: import_data
#| code-summary: "Import GPS tracking data"
#| message: false
#| warning: false

pig_gps <- read_csv("data/KNP_GPS_101526_092931.CSV")

min(pig_gps$`Date & Time [Local]`)

unique(pig_gps$`Device ID`)

pig_gps %>% arrange(`Device Name`)

```

# Clean data

## Order the data and rename columns

```{r}

name_map <- c(
  "159094" = "Duane",
  "159096" = "Chief",
  "158997" = "Miss Piggy",
  "159086" = "Half Pint",
  "159088" = "Razorback",
  "159089" = "Johns",
  "159003" = "Knocknee",
  "159087" = "King David",
  "159083" = "Unknown1",
  "159091" = "Collingwood",
  "159085" = "The Big Mann",
  "159095" = "Doris",
  "152648" = "Spot",
  "152641" = "Brook",
  "159005" = "Puncture",
  "152638" = "Betty",
  "159010" = "Isaac",
  "152643" = "Dora the Explorer",
  "159007" = "Bond",
  "152646" = "Unknown2",
  "159497" = "Big Bertha",
  "159489" = "Mr Stinky",
  "159491" = "Darren",
  "159493" = "Porky",
  "159496" = "Calvin",
  "159490" = "Rosie",
  "111"    = "Man Named Sue",
  "159495" = "Andrew",
  "159492" = "Harry",
  "159494" = "Olivia"
)

pig_gps <- pig_gps %>%  
  group_by(`Device Name`) %>% 
  arrange(`Date & Time [Local]`, .by_group = T) %>% 
  distinct(.keep_all = T) %>%
  mutate(id = `Device ID`,
         name = name_map[as.character(`Device ID`)],
         `Date & Time [Local]` = with_tz(`Date & Time [GMT]`, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"), # i think it's already in Darwin time
         # `Date & Time [Local]` = force_tz(`Date & Time [GMT]`, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"),
         time = `Date & Time [Local]`,
         lon = `Longitude`,
         lat = `Latitude`,
         n_sat = as.integer(str_extract(`Fix Status`, "\\d+(?= SV)")),
         temp = `Temp [C]`) %>% 
  drop_na() %>%
  ungroup() 

```

## Update names from metadata 

```{r}

pig_gps_cols <- pig_gps %>% dplyr::select(id, name, time, lon, lat, n_sat, temp) 
# attr(pig_gps_cols$time, "tzone") <- "Australia/Darwin"
tz(pig_gps_cols$time)

# view the data
head(pig_gps_cols)

pig_gps_ids <- unique(pig_gps_cols$id)

```

# GPS data cleaning

We'll do a basic speed filter from @Shimada2012-tm. But, for some reason the function isn't working, so we'll do it manually below.

```{r}

pig_gps_cols %>% group_by(id) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            start_time = min(time),
            end_time = max(time),
            duration = as.numeric(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "days")))

# # add a qi column for the number of satellites, and drop any rows with NA values
# pig_gps_cols <-  pig_gps_cols %>% 
#   mutate(DateTime = time,
#          qi = n_sat) %>% 
#   drop_na()
# 
# 
# pig_vmax <- SDLfilter::vmax(pig_gps_cols, qi = 5, method = "sample", prob = 0.99)

```

## Setup trajectory

Use the `amt` package to create a trajectory object from the cleaned data. 

```{r}
#| label: make_track
#| code-summary: "Create a trajectory object"

pig_all <- pig_gps_cols %>% mk_track(id = id,
                                           lon,
                                           lat, 
                                           time, 
                                           all_cols = T,
                                           crs = 4326) %>% 
  transform_coords(crs_to = 3112, crs_from = 4326) # Transformation to GDA94 / 
# Geoscience Australia Lambert (https://epsg.io/3112)

pig_all <- pig_all %>% arrange(id, t_)

# plot the data spatially coloured by ID
pig_all %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x_, y = y_, colour = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_classic()

# coloured by the number of satellites
pig_all %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = x_, y = y_, colour = n_sat)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(direction = 1) +
  theme_classic()

```

## Creating a step object 

```{r}

# nest the data by individual
pig_all_nested <- pig_all %>% arrange(id) %>% nest(data = -"id")

pig_all_nested_steps <- pig_all_nested %>%
  mutate(steps = map(data, function(x)
    x %>% track_resample(rate = minutes(30), tolerance = minutes(65)) %>%
      steps_by_burst(keep_cols = "start")))

# unnest the data after creating 'steps' objects
pig_all_steps <- pig_all_nested_steps %>% 
  amt::select(id, steps) %>% 
  amt::unnest(cols = steps) %>% 
  relocate(c(name, n_sat), .before = id) %>% 
  mutate(dt_min = as.numeric(difftime(t2_, t1_, units = "mins")),
         dt_hour = as.numeric(difftime(t2_, t1_, units = "hours"))) %>% 
  filter(dt_min > 20)

hist(as.numeric(pig_all_steps$dt_min))

```

## Calculate the speed for fixes > 5 satellites

```{r}

hist(pig_all_steps$n_sat)
hist(pig_all_steps$sl_)

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% mutate(
  speed = sl_ / as.numeric(difftime(t2_, t1_, units = "hours")) / 1000
) 

# unrealistic step lengths with all satellites
pig_all_steps %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = speed)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  theme_classic()

pig_all_steps %>% filter(n_sat > 5) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = speed)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  theme_classic()

```

```{r}

vmax <- pig_all_steps %>% filter(n_sat > 5) %>% 
  # group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(speed_95 = quantile(speed, 0.95, na.rm = T),
            speed_999 = quantile(speed, 0.999, na.rm = T)
            )

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(less_vmax = speed < vmax$speed_999)

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% filter(less_vmax) %>% 
  select(-less_vmax) %>% 
  arrange(id, t1_)
  
```

# Add covariates

## Time and season

```{r}

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(
    hour = hour(t1_) + minute(t1_)/60 + second(t1_)/3600,
    hour_round = hour(t1_),date = as_date(t1_),
    month = month(t1_),
    season = case_when(month %in% c(11,12, 1, 2, 3, 4) ~ "wet",
                       month %in% seq(5,10) ~ "dry"),
    .after = dt_hour
    )

```

## Filter periods for some individuals

Some pigs appear to drop their collars or die, so we'll trim those parts of the trajectories

### Raw trajectories

```{r}

pig_ids <- unique(pig_all_steps$name)

for(i in 1:length(pig_ids)) {

  plot <- pig_all_steps %>% filter(name == pig_ids[i]) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = t1_, y = sl_)) +
    
    geom_path() +
    labs(title = paste0(pig_ids[i]),
         x = "Time",
         y = "Step length (m)") +
    theme_bw()
  
  print(plot)
  
}

```

Betty, Brook, Unknown 1 and Doris all appear to go stationary. We'll find where they stop moving and filter out those parts.

### Betty ~ 24th Feb 2026

```{r}

pig_all_steps %>% filter(name == "Betty" & 
                           t1_ > lubridate::as_date("2026 02 22") &
                           t1_ < lubridate::as_date("2026 03 01")
                         ) %>% 
  
  ggplot(aes(x = t1_, y = sl_)) +
  geom_path() +
  labs(title = "Betty",
       x = "Time",
       y = "Step length (m)") +
  theme_bw()

```

```{r}
       x = "Time",
```

## Filter the data to remove those periods

```{r}

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>%
  filter(
    case_when(
      name == "Betty" ~ t1_ < as.POSIXct("2026-02-24", tz = "Australia/Darwin"),
      name == "Brook" ~ t1_ < as.POSIXct("2026-02-12", tz = "Australia/Darwin"),
      name == "Doris" ~ t1_ < as.POSIXct("2026-03-10", tz = "Australia/Darwin"),
      name == "Unknown1" ~ t1_ < as.POSIXct("2026-04-30", tz = "Australia/Darwin"),
      .default = TRUE # this ensures that all the other data is kept
    )
  )

```

## Create an sf object of the data

```{r}

# convert to an sf object (x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112)
# and reproject to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet
pig_all_steps_sf <- pig_all_steps %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

```

## Create a bounding box around the pig data to crop the other layers by

```{r}

pig_all_steps_sf

pig_aoi <- st_bbox(pig_all_steps_sf) %>% 
  st_as_sfc() %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 3112) %>% 
  st_buffer(dist = 2500) %>%
  st_bbox() %>% # the buffer creates curved corners so we need to get the bounding box of the buffered area
  st_as_sfc()

# save the bounding box as a shapefile
pig_aoi %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  st_write("mapping/pig_aoi_wgs84.geojson", driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE)

```

# Get time as a deviation from sunrise and sunset

```{r}

# pig_all_steps_sf <- pig_all_steps %>%
#   st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>% 
#   st_transform(crs = 4326) 
# 
# # check lat/lon of the first point
# pig_all_steps_sf$geometry %>% head(1)

lat <- -12.1827   # first GPS location in data
lon <- 132.6758

sun <- suncalc::getSunlightTimes(
  data = pig_all_steps %>% distinct(date) %>% mutate(lat = lat, lon = lon),
  keep = c("sunrise", "sunset"),
  tz = "Australia/Darwin"
)

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>%
  left_join(sun %>% select(date, sunrise, sunset), by = "date") %>%
  mutate(
    time_since_sunrise = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, sunrise, units = "hours")),
    time_until_sunset = as.numeric(difftime(sunset, t1_, units = "hours")),
    day_fraction = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, sunrise, units = "hours")) /
             as.numeric(difftime(sunset, sunrise, units = "hours"))
    
  )

```

## Check that it worked

The `day_fraction` variable is 0 at sunrise and 1 at sunset. Values before sunrise are negative and values after sunset are greater than 1.

```{r}

pig_all_steps %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = day_fraction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0,1), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  scale_y_continuous("Time since sunrise (hours)") +
  scale_x_continuous("Hour of the day", breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 2)) +
  theme_bw()

```

# Add meteorological data

```{r}

max_temp <- dplyr::bind_rows(read_csv("data/weather/MaxTemp_IDCJAC0010_014310_2025_Data.csv"), 
                             read_csv("data/weather/MaxTemp_IDCJAC0010_014310_2026_Data.csv")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(`Product code`, `Days of accumulation of maximum temperature`, Quality)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename("BOM_station" = `Bureau of Meteorology station number`,
                "max_temp" = `Maximum temperature (Degree C)`)

min_temp <- dplyr::bind_rows(read_csv("data/weather/MinTemp_IDCJAC0011_014310_2025_Data.csv"), 
                             read_csv("data/weather/MinTemp_IDCJAC0011_014310_2026_Data.csv")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(`Product code`, `Days of accumulation of minimum temperature`, Quality)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename("BOM_station" = `Bureau of Meteorology station number`,
                "min_temp" = `Minimum temperature (Degree C)`)

rainfall <- dplyr::bind_rows(read_csv("data/weather/Rainfall_IDCJAC0009_014310_2025_Data.csv"), 
                             read_csv("data/weather/Rainfall_IDCJAC0009_014310_2026_Data.csv")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(`Product code`, `Period over which rainfall was measured (days)`, Quality)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename("BOM_station" = `Bureau of Meteorology station number`,
                "rainfall" = `Rainfall amount (millimetres)`)

solar_exposure <- dplyr::bind_rows(read_csv("data/weather/SolarExp_IDCJAC0016_014310_2025_Data.csv"), 
                                   read_csv("data/weather/SolarExp_IDCJAC0016_014310_2026_Data.csv")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-`Product code`) %>% 
  dplyr::rename("BOM_station" = `Bureau of Meteorology station number`,
                "solar_exp" = `Daily global solar exposure (MJ/m*m)`)

weather_data <- dplyr::left_join(max_temp, min_temp) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(rainfall) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(solar_exposure) %>%
  mutate(Date = make_date(Year, as.integer(Month), as.integer(Day)),
         .after = Day) 

```

### How many landcover types are there?

```{r}

unique(landcover_cropped$Veg_class)
length(unique(landcover_cropped$Veg_class))

```

### Create landcover raster layers for each landcover type

One binary (0/1) layer per vegetation class, on the same grid as the Sentinel-2
exports so that all of the covariates stack without any resampling.

```{r}

# Use the ndvi layer as the template grid (20 m, EPSG:3112) so the
# landcover layers line up cell-for-cell with the remotely sensed covariates
lc_template <- deepcopy(ndvi)
lc_template[] <- NA # keep the geometry, drop the values

# Rasterise the polygons; a character field gives a categorical raster, where
# the levels table maps the integer cell values back to the class names
landcover_rast <- rasterize(vect(landcover_cropped), lc_template,
                            field = "Veg_class")
plot(landcover_rast)
lc_levels <- levels(landcover_rast)[[1]]

```

### What frequency do they occur in the data?

```{r}

landcover_vals <- terra::extract(landcover_rast, matrix(c(pig_all_steps$x2_, pig_all_steps$y2_), ncol = 2))
pig_all_steps_covs <- bind_cols(pig_all_steps, landcover_vals)

#            colour = "black",
#            position = "dodge") +

pig_all_steps_covs %>%
  count(Veg_class, season) %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = Veg_class, x = prop, fill = season)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7,
           colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    "Season",
    values = c("wet" = "skyblue", "dry" = "orange"),
    labels = c("wet" = "Wet season", "dry" = "Dry season")) +
  scale_y_discrete("Vegetation Class") +
  scale_x_continuous("Proportion of season's locations", labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.95, 0.95),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.7), colour = NA)
  )

ggsave("outputs/east_alligator_habitat_use_seasonal.png",
       width = 260, height = 150, units = "mm", scale = 0.75, dpi = 1000)
```

### Recode based on their frequency in the data

```{r}

recode_df <- data.frame(
  
  old = c("Bare Ground",
          "Wet Rainforest Springfed", 
          "Water", 
          "Mudflat",
          "Melaleuca Woodland", 
          "Melaleuca Open Woodland",
          "Melaleuca Open Forest", 
          "Melaleuca Closed Forest",
          "Mangrove", 
          "Grassland",
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Eucalypt Woodland", 
          "Eucalypt Open Woodland",
          "Eucalypt Open Forest", 
          "Eucalypt Closed Forest",
          "Dry Rainforest",
          "Seasonally Inundated Treeless Swamp",
          "Wet Rainforest Riparian"),
  
  new = c("Mudflat",
          "Dry Rainforest", 
          "Water", 
          "Mudflat",
          "Melaleuca Woodland", 
          "Melaleuca Woodland",
          "Melaleuca Open Forest", 
          "Melaleuca Closed Forest",
          "Mangrove", 
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Eucalypt Woodland", 
          "Eucalypt Woodland",
          "Eucalypt Open Forest",

          "Dry Rainforest",
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Dry Rainforest")
)

```

### Apply recode to raster

```{r}

lvls <- levels(landcover_rast)[[1]]
lvls <- merge(lvls, recode_df, by.x = "Veg_class", by.y = "old",
              all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)

# check that all the old classes have been recoded to a new class
lvls$new[is.na(lvls$new)] <- lvls$Veg_class[is.na(lvls$new)]

# one new ID per unique merged label
new_lab <- unique(lvls$new)
new_id  <- match(lvls$new, new_lab)

# strip the old categories, then substitute old ID -> new ID
r_num <- terra::deepcopy(landcover_rast)
levels(r_num) <- NULL
landcover_rast_merged <- terra::classify(r_num, cbind(lvls$ID, new_id))

# attach the merged labels
levels(landcover_rast_merged) <- data.frame(ID = seq_along(new_lab),
                                            Veg_class = new_lab)

freq(landcover_rast_merged)   # each name should now appear once
plot(landcover_rast_merged)

```

### Create dummy variables for each landcover type

```{r}

lc_merged_levels <- levels(landcover_rast_merged)[[1]]

# segregate() expands the categorical raster into one 0/1 layer per class
landcover_dummy <- terra::segregate(landcover_rast_merged, other = 0)

# segregate() names the layers by the integer category ID, so map them back to
# the class names, as snake_case so they work as covariate names downstream
names(landcover_dummy) <- lc_merged_levels$Veg_class[
  match(as.integer(names(landcover_dummy)), lc_merged_levels$ID)] %>%
  str_to_lower() %>%
  str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]+", "_") %>%
  paste0("veg_", .)

landcover_dummy

# maxnl defaults to 16, so set it explicitly or the last few classes are dropped
plot(landcover_dummy, col = c("grey90", "darkgreen"), legend = FALSE,
     maxnl = nlyr(landcover_dummy), axes = FALSE,
     mar = c(1.5, 1.5, 2, 1.5))

```

## Extract landcover values at the pig locations

```{r}

covariate_vals <- terra::extract(
  c(ndvi,
    ndwi,
    ndmi,
    landcover_rast_merged,
    landcover_dummy), 
  matrix(c(pig_all_steps$x2_, pig_all_steps$y2_), ncol = 2))
  
pig_all_steps_covs <- bind_cols(pig_all_steps, covariate_vals) 

```

### Plot the vegetation classes with the data

```{r}

landcover_rast_merged_df <- as.data.frame(landcover_rast_merged,
                                          xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = landcover_rast_merged_df, 
              aes(x=x, y=y, fill = Veg_class)) +
  coord_sf() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d("Vegetation") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    "Season",
    values = c("wet" = "skyblue", "dry" = "orange"),
    labels = c("wet" = "Wet season", "dry" = "Dry season")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggsave("outputs/east_alligator_landcover_combined.png",
       width = 250, height = 150, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)

ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = landcover_rast_merged_df, 
              aes(x=x, y=y, fill = Veg_class)) +
  geom_point(data = pig_all_steps,
          aes(x = x1_, y = y1_, colour = season),
          size = 0.1, alpha = 0.25) + 
  coord_sf() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d("Vegetation") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    "Season",
    values = c("wet" = "skyblue", "dry" = "orange"),
    labels = c("wet" = "Wet season", "dry" = "Dry season")) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggsave("outputs/east_alligator_landcover_combined_wGPS.png",
       width = 250, height = 150, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)
```
